$comment: Contract between `gh local-ci` (publisher) and the receipt lookup action in ci.yml (consumer). CI reads this file from trunk; a PR that changes it gets a full CI run. Who may publish is the allowlist compiled into gh local-ci, not this file.

plan.$comment: The same planner CI runs (ci.yml → pnpm utils ci-jobs) with the same inputs: a diff from the merge base (CI uses gh pr diff) and the pull_request event filter. GITHUB_ACTIONS=true makes it write its matrix to GITHUB_OUTPUT. fields.path is projectPath, the project's directory from the repository root, so gh local-ci can skip a rule's prepare when only files inside the tested projects changed.
command: GITHUB_ACTIONS=true GITHUB_OUTPUT={out} pnpm utils ci-jobs --base-ref {mergeBase} --event pull_request

all.$comment: The same planner with no diff, for gh local-ci setup to warm every project a rule could test. Without --base-ref the planner treats every project as changed.
command: GITHUB_ACTIONS=true GITHUB_OUTPUT={out} pnpm utils ci-jobs --event pull_request

prepare.$comment: Mirrors setup-woocommerce-monorepo with install='<project>...' and build-type=dependencies. Re-validate and update mirrors.sha256 when that action changes.

eligible.$comment: Every test:js is jest, which defaults to cores-1 workers per invocation. gh local-ci sizes {workers} for the machine it runs on, from a budget the jobs share; on a Mac with more than one core tier, from the fastest tier only. A fixed 4 per job oversubscribed an M5 Max's 6 fast cores: the seven jest jobs of one diff took 83 s, against 65 to 73 s sized by the tool.

prepare.$comment: Mirrors setup-woocommerce-monorepo with install='<project>...' and build-type=dependencies.

eligible.$comment: CI skips setup-php for build-type=dependencies, so PHPStan runs on the runner's PHP 8.3 whatever the job name says; the name's version picks the neon config. run-phpstan.sh installs into and then deletes tasks/phpstan/vendor, so one project's two PHPStan jobs run in turn.

prepare.$comment: Mirrors setup-woocommerce-monorepo with install='<project>...' and build-type=dependencies.

eligible.$comment: PHPUnit without wp-env. The test job installs PHP 7.4 for every unit:php job (setup-woocommerce-monorepo's default), so this runs on 7.4 whatever the job name says. gh local-ci runs a rule that names an image only with --docker, so a receipt for it never comes from the host's PHP. Jobs with a test environment have [WP ...] in their names: the core plugin's are the php-cells rule's, and the rest are left to CI.

prepare.$comment: Mirrors setup-woocommerce-monorepo with install='<project>...' and build-type=backend.

eligible.$comment: Core plugin PHP cells only; grow `exclude` when packages/php/* gain unit:php jobs. The driver resolves each cell's PHP and WordPress versions from the planner itself. Opt-in: four cells run one after another, about 25 min. Native runs only: each cell starts wp-env, which needs a Docker daemon that a --docker container does not have.

prepare.$comment: Ports 92xx so the worktree's wp-env cells never collide with cells started from the developer's checkout.

docker.$comment: For run --docker. gh local-ci builds each image from .github/local-ci/php.Dockerfile as committed, and rebuilds it only when that directory or its args change. The default image is PHP 8.3 with Composer and Node, as on the ubuntu-24.04 runner, because pnpm install runs composer install in the postinstall of plugins/woocommerce, the beta tester and four PHP packages. The pnpm store lives on the per-clone HOME volume, so no mounts are needed.

toolchain.$comment: CI's Node: setup-woocommerce-monorepo runs setup-node with node-version-file .nvmrc. Locally every job runs through pnpm, which uses useNodeVersion from pnpm-workspace.yaml whatever node is on PATH, so the check asks pnpm, not PATH. pnpm is not checked: action-setup reads it from packageManager in package.json, and expectFrom takes a file that holds only the version. Nor is PHP: the PHPStan and PHP 8.1 rules run only under --docker, where the image is the toolchain, and each PHP cell runs on wp-env's PHP.
